content.title: About
content.content: Squirrel is a light dry snack made from whole grains roasted to a golden crisp. It has a mild nutty flavor and a crunchy texture, perfect for a quick bite any time of day.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The snack is named “Squirrel” because its shape resembles a tiny nut.
Only whole grains are used, with no artificial flavorings added.
The product is gluten‑free and suitable for people with gluten intolerance.
Squirrel can be stored for up to 12 months when kept properly.
It contains a small amount of salt but no added sugar.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Its protein content makes the snack a good source of energy and helps maintain muscle mass.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: The absence of added sugar helps control blood glucose levels.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Contains monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Grain allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to the ingredients.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: People monitoring sodium intake should limit the amount of this snack.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although light, it still provides calories, so portion control is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Squirrel can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, added to salads, yogurts, muesli, or used as a crunchy topping for soups and stews.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the package in a dry, cool, dark place. After opening, keep the bag tightly sealed to maintain crunchiness and prevent fat oxidation.
